problem: Map-based goal-oriented navigation methods rely on complete semantic BEV maps and are unreliable when reasoning about unobserved regions. Prior generative map completion (e.g. diffusion over semantic maps only) ignores the consistency between known and unknown obstacle layouts, causing room boundary drift and semantic hallucination.
motivation: Robots start in unknown environments and only ever hold partial maps, so goals outside the observed area cannot be localized directly. BEV maps have large free space and sparse object pixels, and structure (obstacles) stabilizes early diffusion denoising, so obstacle priors should guide semantic completion. A plug-in completion module would help any map-based strategy (RL, LLM-based, single or multi-robot) without retraining the strategy.
key_idea: Train a two-stage DDPM/SDE diffusion model that first completes the obstacle map and then uses it (via SPADE modulation) to guide denoising of the semantic map, producing a predicted label map from which goal clusters are found and fed to any navigation strategy.
insight: Obstacle-guided semantic denoising is what matters: removing the obstacle network G_phi drops SR by 2.4/4.6/4.8 points (ON/IIN/MRON) and PSNR from 34.284 to 30.437, and dropping the obstacle map from the label map drops SR further (3.9/4.9/4.5). Against IR-SDE and StrDiffusion on MRON, PLMD gets SR 0.762 vs 0.698/0.729 and PSNR 34.284 vs 29.895/31.486. Oracle GT label maps give much higher SR (e.g. 0.742 vs 0.665 ON HM3D_v0.2), so map completion quality is still the bottleneck.
method: Label map construction: merges obstacle (occupancy/free) and semantic maps into color-palette-rendered visualized label maps, cropped around the robot, with unexplored regions masked.

Data collection: FBE exploration for 500 steps over 2,000 episodes, storing partial maps every 25 steps paired with the final explored map as GT; RedNet segmentation, so training is not from GT semantics (HM3D_v0.1: 238,800 pairs, 8:2 split).
Obstacle-map diffusion G_phi: mean-reverting SDE (IR-SDE style) DDPM whose terminal state is the masked map plus noise, pre-trained first, then frozen.

Semantic-map diffusion with SPADE: the semantic network conditions on the obstacle state c_{tau-1} via spatially-adaptive normalization, with gamma/beta computed from the obstacle map, inside a U-Net without GroupNorm or self-attention; T=100.

Localization strategy: predicted label maps are searched for goal-colored pixels, clustered with HDBSCAN (N=5), and the goal is chosen by a score of density 0.5, size 0.4 and distance 0.1; falls back to the original strategy if no valid cluster; observed regions stay anchored to sensor data.
Plug-and-play scheduling: PLMD activates at navigation step 100 and repeats every 50 steps, used with OpenFMNav (ON HM3D_v0.1), FBE/IEVE (IIN), and MCoCoNav (ON HM3D_v0.2 and MRON).

setting.backbone: Two U-Net diffusion models (obstacle + semantic with SPADE) trained from scratch, plugged into existing strategies (OpenFMNav with Qwen2.5-VL 7B, MCoCoNav, IEVE/SemExp RL policy, FBE)
setting.training_data: Label map pairs collected via FBE in HM3D_v0.1 train scenes (40,000 raw pairs, 238,800 processed; 191,040 train / 47,760 val); MP3D variant with 471,900 pairs; RedNet-segmented semantics; no retraining of the navigation strategy
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + pose/GPS, built into top-down semantic and obstacle maps
setting.action_space: low-level discrete (forward 0.25 m, turn 30°, look up/down, stop) with long-term map goals reached by Fast Marching Method
setting.privileged: none at test time for PLMD (the 'GT Label Maps' row is an oracle upper bound); IIN success uses an oracle-visibility criterion

numbers.extra: PLMD trained on HM3D_v0.1 FBE data; activates at step 100, every 50 steps

numbers.eval_set_note: HM3D_v0.1, 20 val scenes, 6 categories (own train/val split of v0.1 scenes)
numbers.extra: no RL policy; HM3D_v0.1 with own scene split
RL policy; success radius 1.0 m with oracle visibility

numbers_note: Multi-robot ObjectNav results (HM3D_v0.2: SR 0.762/SPL 0.406; MP3D: 0.591/0.382) are reported in Table 1 but MRON is not a canonical benchmark name here, so they are not listed above. Split names are not given explicitly; HM3D_v0.2 validation and other validation scenes are labeled 'val'.
results: PLMD plugged into existing strategies improves over the best learned/zero-shot baselines: ON HM3D_v0.1 SR 0.656 (SSL+RL) vs SGM 0.602, IIN SR 0.776 vs IEVE 0.702, and MRON SR 0.762/SPL 0.406 vs MCoCoNav 0.716/0.387. The GT label-map upper bound is far higher (e.g. ON HM3D_v0.2 SR 0.742), and PLMD beats IR-SDE and StrDiffusion in PSNR and navigation.
limitations: Predictions are imperfect and there remains a large gap to GT label maps; wrong hallucinated goals could cause errors.
Adds significant inference cost (10-20% of episode time, up to ~1.5x total with Grounded SAM) and runs only in simulation (Jetson tested but no real robot).
Only indoor HM3D/MP3D; the activation schedule and cluster weights are hand-tuned, and in ON the SR of some settings is slightly below baseline.
